room-0-0-0.description:

of what was once smooth paving. Cracks are evident everywhere in the rocks that
were used in the road. A thick patch of brush grows to the north, clinging to
the meagre shelter offered by a small plateau. The road continues to the east
and south.

room-6-0-0.name: Glittering Stream
room-6-0-0.description:
The water of this stream runs clear and very cold, having originated high on
the mountains. It is not too deep, and its stone bed can clearly be seen, its
shape dancing with the refraction of the water. Both banks are covered with
thick, green grass interrupted only occasionally by an isolated large rock.
Small minnow schools can be seen flitting about.

room-7-0-0.name: Shallow Crossing
room-7-0-0.description:
This part of the stream at first glance appears quite deep, but upon closer
inspection the bottom silt can be made out quite clearly. The banks can be seen
in the distance. The water is very cold and clear as it runs by swiftly. The
occasional school of minnows flits by and larger darker shapes can be discerned
which can only be larger fish. Plains can be seen to the east and west, and
beyond them hills which eventually join a large mountain range to the south.

room-5-1-0.description:

north. The thin topsoil that rests atop a rocky substrate is able to retain so

fertile.

large rock formation blocks the way, making it impossible to continue in that

room-6-2-0.name: Lightly Wooded Hillside
room-6-2-0.description:
Tall, slender evergreens grow in abundance here, yet never drawing so close
to one-another as to constitute a true forest. The ground alternates between
a deep litter of old pine needles close by the trees, and thick, green grasses
that bend in the wind howling between the trunks. An occasional stump stands
amid the grasses, covered with moss, and attesting to the age of this grove.
The hills continue far to the south while slowly descending in the west. To
the north and east the descent is more marked, as the hills give way to the
plains that stretch out below.

room-0-4-0.name: Small Camp on a Plateau
room-0-4-0.description:
The small trail takes a sharp turn here bordering a rocky promontory that
boasts a commanding view of the plains stretching out below. Little vegetation
is to be seen on this stony table, which is so exposed to the blustery winds
howling throughout these lands, that no topsoil worth speaking of remains.
Still, a few tiny flowers sprout from cracks in the rock. Many, however, have
been crushed underfoot, just one sign that this area is used as a camp.

room-1-4-0.name: Brushy Plains
room-1-4-0.description:

to the more open plains hereabouts. A rocky shelf stands to the south and west,
forcing the chill winds that assail these lands upward and away from the
ground. The result is a thicker layer of topsoil that can better support the
vegetation.

room-0-5-0.name: Rising Trail at the Foot of a High Cliff
room-0-5-0.description:
The trail bends to the east and to the north here, running for a short time
along the foot of a high cliff, climbing steadily as it does so. The mountain
range to the south is tall and imposing, and it is not possible to scale its
heights from this location. The topsoil is thin, probably as a result of the
punishing winds that torment these lands month after month. No vegetation
thrives here except for a few small, flowers that peep up through cracks in the
rock, and there is little to mark the trail from the stony ground alongside it.

room-4-5-0.name: Lush Valley
room-4-5-0.description:
From the west a steep, bushy slope quickly descends. The overgrown, thorny
thicket that covers its flanks seems to extend for miles both to the north and
to the south. Extending eastward is a lush vale where grasses of all types grow
in great abundance. Tucked away between a range of hills to the north and a
tall mountain spur to the south, this valley is provided with ample protection
from the elements, making it richer in vegetation than any area for many miles.

room-6-5-0.name: Deep in a Lush Valley
room-6-5-0.description:
The valley extends for some miles both to the east and west, and reaches to the
foot of the mountains in the south. The deep, loamy soil evidently has an ample
supply of water, for lush, green grass covers the ground all around. A few
scattered trees and many bushes also dot the landscape. This secluded valley
would make excellent farmland if anyone were to settle here. But as it lies so
very far from civilisation this would seem an unlikely prospect.

worn in the grass that indicate larger animals make their way around here. The
hills to the north can be reached from here following a sharp ascent and the
mountains to the south rise up some distance away.

larger fissures in the walls have definitely been widened after the fact.

Keyword "az-review" (lgit: info/zones/188/az-review)

Az review of zone 188

Reviewer: Rogon

/R = Rogon
/O = Orlanth
/E = Ellessar

Reviewed: 0-70

OPEN ISSUES:
============


FIXED ISSUES:
=============






COMPLETED ISSUES:
=================
KWS:
 Clean up all old/unused or leftovers. Move them to oldkeywords.
 This stands out as not belonging or needed or made irrelevant:
  mob_sentry, rohan, newarea
  IF Ellessar needs a place to store various ideas and notes for himself,
  make a keyword named ellessar_stuff and put it there.
/R OK

 TODO keyword has things in it. Complete these. If they can't be implemented
 until opening, write everything needed and put them in z184 superzone-todo in
 the section todo on opening.
/R OK

 I see a m-req-yell keyword but I don't see this request listed in the
 superzone-mudlle.
/R OK

 9: Missing "in" or something similar in the prep.
/R OK

 16: Why can't this bush load hollyberries? (o1905)
/R OK

 28: Desc: YOUR detected, as bad as 'you'. Tweak to remove reference to
     the reader.
/R OK

Climbs: They're all 50%. Maybe some should be easier to let lowbie
 BNs climb too? And casters? :)
/R Could you tell me what you did with the climbs?
/E 188:56 + 188:46 climbs changed to 20%
/R Ok.. Bit lazy though.

 11: Edesc down. Canid claw marks?
/R Not edited. No comment. Not sure how to read this as moved to fixed.
/E canid is form of the adjective "Canine" meaning dog
/R OK

 59: Desc. YOU radar giving alerts.
/R OK

 65: This room seems to have the default prep. in the@Deep in a Lush Valley
     It reads a bit weird.
/R OK

 78: Lib: This lib isn't set up correctly. It has the same message twice, and
     one of them does not have punctuation. Let's fix that.
/R OK

 93: Den should probably be nomob? Or do we want sparrows and frogs to wander
     in when left open?
/R OK

 137: `-- 7   Door    lock north (door) (pick 30..40)
  The locking of this door should probably not be a child of the Uruk loading?
/R OK

 153: What's the purpose of the connection west? Also, should it really be
      scoutable? (of course it shouldn't!)
/R OK
Recall spot: Is 188:59 a good recall spot for the good side?
/E Apparently Recall Good: 95:93 Evil: 188:59 is the current. Think we're good.
/R OK

Where is the mudlle request for the webbed wall?
/R Is there a reason it doesn't accept fire as a way to destroy it? It's
   sort of the established web-destroyer in MUME.
/E It's there, m-req-cobweb. It's a door not a web so fire doesn't work the
same way. If it requires changing probably best just to remove it.
/R OK

 64: The redressed tree. Are you happy with this?
     The "apple tree" is taken out of the long desc, but since the full desc
     is unchanged, it's still there in the full desc.
/R As far as I can see, you just ignored this and moved it to fixed.
/E happy with the way it is. It's better to not have apples in shortdesc since
no apples load on it.
/R OK

 49: Let's discuss this delayed door.
/E sure, sounds like you approve
/R OK

 108: Keeping SILENT here on the map. I'm a tad skeptical still.
/E thought this meant it's good to go.
/R OK

 138: Sentries: Someone -will- remark on the fact that they are sleeping
      holding their bows.
/E It's common practice to sleep holding you weapon in the military. Makes
sense
to keep the way it is.
/R OK

38: Watchroom lib: The distances for this room makes no sense (49 being
     closer than 39. The distances are for physical distance from the
     watcher. Always.


   -36-46-
     |  |
    37-47 57-
        |  |
    38-48 58\
        |  | d
-29-39-49 59


 -1 = 38
  0 = 37 48 39
  1 = 29 36 47 58 49
  2 = 46 57 59

  extra: 19 26 56 67 100

Ok let's try this again. Above I've entered that I think is logical. What
we can discuss is if you should be able to see the mountains opposite the
watch room (above icedoor).

These things I consider incorrect:
    46 should be added to north, distance 2.
    north:
      dist 2 188:36 (Ancient Broken Road)
      Since 37 is 0, 36 should be 1
    south:
      dist 2 188:29 (Old Road)
      Since 39 is 0, 29 should be 1

If we add icedoor, these things should be added:
 58 distance 1
 57, 59 distance 2

On top of this, these rooms need the lib to report to :38, but not
be listed in 38: 67 (if we do icedoor watch).
                 100 (if we do icedoor watch).
                 56 (to let you see enterings in 46)

/E Should be fixed as you said
/R OK

m-req-bruzhor.body:
Keyword "m-req-bruzhor" (lgit: info/zones/188/m-req-bruzhor)

21-Feb-2022
Orlanth

Mudlle request for Bruzhor
==========================


General
=======
Bruzhor will work as a quest giver for the darkies. He lives in reworked
"icedoor" area in the zone 188, although the door name doesn't exist anymore.


Outline
=======
1. He is friendly to tarks, bns and trolls.
2. There can be other troll mobs that may hit tarkhnarb orcs and black
numenoreans.
3. He tells a story about the ABR area, elven caravans and the goblins.
4. He wants the head of goblin leader who lives in the caves in the zone 318.
5. When player gives the head, quest is completed.
6. Bruzhor gives a treasure to player who gave the head of goblin leader.
7. Afterwards he tells a short story about wild-eyed man.
8. This quest is a repeatable type quest.


Treasure for completing the quest
=================================
3 golds always
2 orkish draughts, 50 % chance per draught



Quest stories
=============
Story 1. Caravan attack/elves

Story 2. Goblins: his job is to turn them to Sauron's side. Although
Sauron can indirectly influence them, they have not fully succumbed to his
will. Bruzhor wants the goblin leader dead, so that he can affect the tribe and
hopefully turn the next leader to obey Sauron's will.

Story 3. Details of the quest

Story 4. Wild-eyed man

m-req-minewall.body:
Keyword "m-req-minewall" (lgit: info/zones/188/m-req-minewall)

Overview:
=========
This is a mudlle that causes a partial collapse of a wall and thus connects
two different rooms. It's extremely similar to /i z 290 m-req-minewall.


Involved rooms/mobs/objects:
============================
28632 [188:121] Hovel within the Rock
28628 [188:117] Cave under the Mountain

o1212 a round stone

Details:
========
- Mining in room 188:121 has a 30% chance to cause the wall to collapse.

- There is a 10% chance to load a round stone

- When it collapses, there's 3 messages:
  - Start, instantly when collapsing start.
  - Middle, after 5 seconds.
  - End, after 10 seconds.

- There are messages sent to room on the other side as well:
  - Startother
  - Middleother
  - Endother

- At End, when collapsing is complete, the two rooms are connected.
  - South from 188:121 leads to 188:117. (One way)
  - Replace Edescs.

- When z319 resets, if the rooms are connected, the connection might be
  removed. This only happens if the zone is empty of mortals.

- Continue trying to disconnect the walls every time either zone resets
  until successful (there was a zone reset when both zones were empty.)

Messages:
=========
Edesc south from 188:121 as default (no connection):
The wall is comprised of shale. Any echoing sound can be heard coming from the
other side of the wall indicating there may be something on the other side.

Edesc South from 188:121 when open:
The shale wall has collapsed, revealing a small crawlspace beyond.

Edesc North from 188:117 when open:
A small hole has opened high in the rock above.

Start Message
    act_room(ORIGIN_ROOM,
             "Dust starts to fall from the ceiling and a loud rumbling sound"
             + " can be heard to the south.",
             "A loud rumbling sound starts to echo to the south.");
    echo_room(DESTINATION_ROOM,
              "A muffled rumbling sound can be heard to the north.");

Middle Message
      act_room(ORIGIN_ROOM,
               "Cracks begin to form in the southern wall, and large chunks of"
               + " rubble break away and fall.",
               "The rumbling sound grows louder.");
      act_room(DESTINATION_ROOM,
               "Cracks begin to form in the northern wall, and large chunks of"
               + " rubble break away and fall.",
               "The rumbling sound grows louder.");

End Message
      act_room(ORIGIN_ROOM,
               "A section of the southern wall collapses into a cloud of dust,"
               + " revealing a hole.",
               "After a final thunderous roar, the noise suddenly dies down.");
      act_room(DESTINATION_ROOM,
               "A large chunk of rock becomes dislodged high up in the
                northern wall and crashes down"
               + " revealing a hole.",
               "After a final thunderous roar, the noise suddenly dies down.");

Overview:
=========
This is a mudlle that causes a partial collapse of a wall and thus connects
two different rooms. It's extremely similar to /i z 290 m-req-minewall.


Involved rooms/mobs/objects:
============================

28630 [188:119] Disused Tunnel

Details:
========
- Mining in room 188:162 and 188:119 has a 30% chance to cause the wall to
  collapse.

- There is a 10% chance to load a whetstone

- When it collapses, there's 3 messages:
  - Start, instantly when collapsing start.
  - Middle, after 5 seconds.
  - End, after 10 seconds.

- There are messages sent to room on the other side as well:
  - Startother
  - Middleother
  - Endother

- At End, when collapsing is complete, the two rooms are connected.
  - West from 188:162 leads to 188:119.

- When z188 resets, if the rooms are connected, the connection might be
  removed. This only happens if the zone is empty of mortals.

m-req-trader.body:
Keyword "m-req-trader" (lgit: info/zones/188/m-req-trader)

30-Jun-2022
Orlanth

Mudlle request for Elven trader
===============================
This is a mudlle request of the elven trader, who lives in the zone 188 in a
hidden Dúnadan outpost. He used to be a skilled elven ranger, but after he lost
his arm in the battle against enemies, he is helping Dúnedain, watching the
pass in southern Ancient broken road, and also works as a trader.

General
=======
The elven trader is the mob number 1807.

A {disfigured elven trader} looks about with watchful eyes]

He will work as a quest giver for whitie players.

This quest has no level requirement, and it's a repeatable type of quest.

The mob always approaches the first player in the room.

The trader loads in the room 37187 (188:128).

Details
=======
- States a player can be in:
  - Not taken a quest
  - Taken a quest, not completed
  - Completed quest, in cooldown (before can redo)
  - Completed quest at least once
  - Declined, in cooldown


This mudlle request is split into seven main parts:

  1. GREETING: Mob's initial reaction to players entering.

  2. QUESTION1: Trader questions if player is interested in hearing a story.
     Skip STORY1, QUESTION1 and QUESTION2 if player is redoing the quest.

  3. STORY1: Story about goblins attack and bandits.

  4. QUESTION2: Trader asks the player if he/she is willing to help return a
     heirloom (take the quest).

  5. STORY 2/QUESTION3: Alternative story if player has completed the quest at
     least once.

  6. QUESTION4: Player returns to the mob. If he/she has the heirloom, go to
     FINISH. Otherwise
     SAY Please come back when you have the heirloom, and good luck.

  7. FINISH, the player returns the heirloom:
       

Outline
=======
1. The trader was working as a guard for an unfortunate caravan, that got
attacked by trolls, and later by goblins. First the trolls attacked the
caravan on ABR in south pass, and then later goblins attacked the remains
of the caravan. After that, bandits killed some goblins and stole a part
of the loot.
2. The trader and the wild-eyed man (m1840) survived the attacks, and a couple
of other elves.
3. The elven chests were stolen, and wild-eyed man has the only key that fits
the chests. 
4. There is a heirloom in one of the chests, at Gukk, Bhogh or bandit leader.
5. Mission is to retrieve a heirloom.
6. When a heirloom is returned, quest is completed.
7. Player gets points towards Lorien citizenship
8. This quest is a repeatable type quest.
9. The trader sells some herbs
10. The trader's stock is reset when someone brings a heirloom


Treasure for completing the quest
=================================
- 60 points towards Lorien cit
- also the trader's stock is reset

Trader's stock
==============
Trader only sells, he doesn't buy herbs.

Herb               á Price
----               -------
1 ginseng          30 gold
1 bulbous root     30 gold
1 foxtail          30 gold
3 athelas          5 gold


Details, messages
=================
If the player is in cooldown, no reaction.

Cooldown is 120 rl minutes.

GREETING:
SAY Hello there traveller! I see you are a friend with dúnedain.

If redoing, SAY Hello again, $n!

QUESTION1:
SAY I too found refugee here, and only barely survived by the help of dúnedain.
SAY Do you want to hear my story?

DECLINED:
SAY Perhaps other time then.
Add cooldown to the player.
Go to END.

ACCEDED:

STORY1:
SAY So I was travelling in a caravan with a companion of elves from the
beautiful city of Lothlórien, meaning to bring a precious item, a tunic,
from Lady Galadriel to Elrond, the lord of Rivendell.

SAY Also other precious items were included from other noble families to their
family members in Rivendell.

SAY We had travelled for many days, and passed already the Hithaeglir also
called as Misty Mountains via a secret elven trade route.

SAY We were travelling to the north along the ancient broken road some east of
us. It had been a sunny day, and we were planning to stop for the night, as the
sun went down.

SAY Then it happened...
Trader sniffs sadly.

SAY Seemingly out of nowhere we were attacked by a horde of goblins. They were
armed with crude weapons like daggers and clubs, certainly no match for our
fine elven and dúnedain guards and their weapons.

SAY Or so we thought.

SAY They came in numbers, our guards fought bravely and killed tens of goblins.

SAY We fought seemingly for hours. But they kept coming and coming, more and
more goblins screaming and cackling horribly.

SAY Finally the inevitable happened, our guards fell down. I myself was wounded
badly, my arm but a torso now, but I still managed to flee in the chaos of
battle and hide in the wilderness.

SAY Before I escaped, I also noticed one of the Dúnedain guards fleeing from
the battle grasping something in his hands. If not for his cowardice, we may
have survived!

SAY Nevertheless... the bloodshed was immense... I think I and that coward
dúnadan were the only survivors.

SAY I would have died in the wilderness, but the dúnedain rangers found me and
brought me here. They have been watching these passes for ages, and told me
that we were attacked by the goblins that live somewhere in the deeps of
the mountains to the east of us. These goblins attack anyone, and they have
been seen killing other orcs too.

SAY They also found tracks of unknown people and trolls in the area! Lots of
goblin corpses were found some miles away from the place we fought. I am
thankful for this, but it looked like one tracks lead to a camp where some
evil men are living. They are a big trouble for people travelling the road,
killing and robbing as many as they can. Apparently they are no friends with
goblins either. Otherwise, the trolls are even more dangerous if you meet them!
Lots of all kinds of foul creatures live in these areas, there is also talk of
giants living far up in the snowy mountains.

QUESTION2
SAY There was some precious heirloom in the loots that the goblins stole.
SAY I would need help from someone like you to return it, but beware,
    it's going to be dangerous!
SAY I don't know where they are, but it's possible that the traitorous
    dúnadan knows something, or the goblins took the item in the mountain
    or the bandits have them. That's all I know about it.
SAY There were also precious items in some elven chests, especially the ebony
tunic, but there was only one key that fitted them, and sadly it was lost in
the fight.

SAY Do you want to help me get the heirlooms back?
ACCEDED:
SAY Great! Please come back to me when you have the item, you should recognize
it when you see it.

DECLINED:
SAY Perhaps other time then.
Add cooldown to the player.
Go to END.

STORY 2/QUESTION3
SAY So, do you want to help me again? There is one more heirloom missing from
the shipment.
ACCEDED:
SAY Great! Please come back to me when you have the item, you should recognize
it when you see it.

DECLINED:
SAY Perhaps other time then.
Add cooldown to the player.
Go to END.

QUESTION4: Player returns to the mob.
SAY Hello, $n. Have you found the heirloom?
No:
SAY Please come back when you have the heirloom, and good luck.
Yes: go to FINISH

FINISH
Mob smiles to the player.
SAY Thank you for returning this to me, I will make sure to return it to its
rightful owner or next of kin. Lady Galadriel and lord Celeborn are thankful
for bringing this item back.
Player gets 60 points towards Lorien citizenship.

SAY I have found some rare herbs, if you are willing to buy. Please take a
look at my offerings.
o8275 (ginseng root)     30 gold
o8269 (bulbous root)     30 gold
o8266 (foxtail)          30 gold

END

CURRENT MUDLLE IMPLEMENTATION BY JAHARA:


An elven trader says 'Although it pains me to talk of it, I shall recall the
battle.'

An elven trader shudders, collects himself, and recounts his tale from the
beginning.

An elven trader says 'We begin in fair Lórien, a land whose peace is guarded by
skilled Marchwardens.'

An elven trader stands slightly taller, eyes gleaming with obvious pride.

An elven trader says 'You stand before one, a skilled Elf-ranger who guarded
dutifully against the Shadow.'

An elven trader says 'It is because of Elven blood that the orcs of Moria were
kept at bay.'

An elven trader defiantly raises the stump of his missing arm.

An elven trader says 'I am now retired, but such sacrifices were necessary to
guard the West.'

An elven trader says 'I continue to serve by protecting the trade between
Imladris and Lórien, over the Redhorn Pass.'

An elven trader says 'Our caravan leaves often, bearing goods and gifts,
innocent passengers, and faces many dangers
along the way.'

An elven trader says 'You see, the route is beset by goblins, wicked men, snow
giants, and stone trolls.'

An elven trader says 'We travel non-stop until we reach the safety of this
camp.'

An elven trader says 'You can expect excellent protection and companionship
against the danger-infested wilds here.'

An elven trader says 'But now, there are fewer of us...'

An elven trader says 'For it was during our last trip that things went terribly
wrong.'

An elven trader's voice cracks and his expression becomes more morose.

An elven trader says 'Sorry, I can still hear the screams of my companions...'

An elven trader says 'We normally have little trouble routing the rabble that
bother us.'

An elven trader says 'This time it was different.'

An elven trader says 'Huge trolls assaulted us; taller than a man, covered in
horny scales, able to endure sun.'

An elven trader says 'They came at us in the pass, and even with the Dúnedain
at our sides, the caravan broke and goods
were stolen.'



An elven trader bows his head in sad remembrance.

An elven trader says 'So many innocent lives were lost.'

An elven trader says 'I am searching for a key that goes to the stolen chests
that the caravan carried.'

An elven trader says 'I witnessed a Dúnadan pick it up during the battle, but I
cannot find him in the camp.'

An elven trader says 'If you find the key and any chests, please retrieve any
remaining heirlooms and return them to
me.'

An elven trader says 'I will make sure the heirlooms are returned to their
rightful owner or next of kin.'

An elven trader says 'Any help will gain you favor with the Golden Wood.'

GIVE ITEM:
An elven trader bows deeply.
An elven trader says 'Thank you for returning this precious heirloom.'
An elven trader says 'I will make sure this is returned to its rightful owner
or next of kin.'

m1880_bruzhor.body:
Keyword "m1880_bruzhor" (lgit: info/zones/188/m1880_bruzhor)

Overview:
=========
This is an idea for a troll mob that resides in the z188 ABR rework.

He functions as the new guardian of the new icedoor area. His primary purpose
is to provide a defensive area for trolls passing through and provides a small
quest for orcs, trolls, and bns involving the goblin caves.

**NOTE**
His stats are based off of Khuzur. He dropped a level, dropped a considerable
amount of ob/defensive stats but gained a very slight amount of base damage.

History:
========
More ruthless than his brother, Khuzur, who resides farther south, Bruzhor the
troll delights in the pain of others. He also harbors a deep hatred of the weak
tribe of goblins and their cheiftain, Bohg, who live in the adjacent mountains.
He leads his own ragtag militia of trolls and orcs near the Ancient Broken Road
pass, catching poor victims who might wander into their caves looking for
shelter.

Id:[],  Instances:[],  Mudlled:[Yes],  Owner:[Ellessar]
Keywords:[Bruzhor cruel troll olog olog-hai]
Short description:[Bruzhor the Cruel]
Long description: Bruzhor the Cruel is standing here
Description:
Tall and proud this troll flexes his huge muscles with every movement. His skin
is dark grey save for a white blemish starting at his left shoulder and ending
over his left eye. He wears a scowl upon his face, and scars in the shape of
claw marks streak up and down his arms.

Keyword "m1880_bruzhor" (lgit: info/zones/188/m1880_bruzhor)

Overview:
=========
This is an idea for a troll mob that resides in the z188 ABR rework.

He functions as the new guardian of the new icedoor area. His primary purpose
is to provide a defensive area for trolls passing through and provides a small
quest for orcs, trolls, and bns involving the goblin caves.

**NOTE**
His stats are based off of Khuzur. He dropped a level, dropped a considerable
amount of ob/defensive stats but gained a very slight amount of base damage.

History:
========
More ruthless than his brother, Khuzur, who resides farther south, Bruzhor the
troll delights in the pain of others. He also harbors a deep hatred of the weak
tribe of goblins and their cheiftain, Bohg, who live in the adjacent mountains.
He leads his own ragtag militia of trolls and orcs near the Ancient Broken Road
pass, catching poor victims who might wander into their caves looking for
shelter.

is dark grey save for a white blemish starting at his left shoulder and ending
over his left eye. He wears a scowl upon his face, and scars in the shape of
claw marks streak up and down his arms.

Zone keyword "boulders(mudlle)" (lgit: info/zones/188/boulders(mudlle)):
188:38 is a mountain room that overlooks a road through the mountain pass. It
will be set up as a very limited watch_tower, watching the road rooms along the
pass.

In this room there will be a number of boulders, small enough to be moved, yet
large enough that this will take some time and effort. The boulders can only
be pushed over the low-spot on the overlook, therefore only room 188:48 will 
be targeted by the trap.

When a player opts to "push boulder" a (slightly) delayed action will start -
it is interruptable if the player takes any other action (including simply 
hitting [rtn]) but if completed will drop a boulder onto the target room. There
is a (dex_checked) chance that any player or mob in the room below will avoid
being hit, but if they are hit they take quite serious damage. 

Once supply of boulders is exhausted, no more can be pushed over the edge.

Should be roughly analogous to Fornost oil pot.

Zone keyword "brainstorming" (lgit: info/zones/188/brainstorming):
This keyword will be used for connection ideas between the southern ABR zones.
1.
This is in zone 182 - 
As the road now know as ABR was built, a small keep was built where is crossed
on of the tributarys to Bruinen. Small farms grew up around the castle. As the
evil once again began to move, the keep was deserted. It did not take long
until the forces of Sauron moved in, at first, old spirits and wraiths of the
long dead inhabitants, and later orcs, as Sauron started preparing for wars.
One of the earlier lords were buried just southeast of the keep, and his grave
was desecrated by the leader ob the orcs, trying out his magic in a foul
experiment.
Elrond soon learned of the orcs living here, and sent two scouts to keep an
eye open for troop movements.

Zone keyword "bridgeidea" (lgit: info/zones/188/bridgeidea):
The original idea from Quillis is below. I modified it since I felt like a 
bridge that spanned the 2+ smiles between two mountain rooms, crossing over
(above) the intervening road room was unrealistic. However, I have retained
the spirit of the idea by adding the bridge between two _adjacent_ mountain
rooms (77, 78) and including an off-grid gully into which the traveller on
the bridge might jump or fall. The gully also provides the second entrance
to the "icedoor caves" that are being copied across (loosely) from the old
zone 93.

Old notes from Quillis:      
                           
Here is a summary
I thought an old rickety bridge between 2 peaks would be a nice feature. This
could be a timed dt (the wind blows the pc off eventually), or a dt that is
triggered by # of ppl. The room i used was 188:109, with hidden exits e and w.
Whether or not it might work, the room itself provides a 'bridge' between one
half of the zone to the other. I have tried to split the zone longitudinally
using the road, with some justifications in the room descriptions. It makes
traversing the road and the zone slightly more dangerous, and a little bit
more challenging to explore/fight in by providing some bottlenecks. The bridge
adds some other possibilities. Though this is all pending approval.
Q

Zone keyword "mandor_notes" (lgit: info/zones/188/mandor_notes):
Mail 92 : z187 @Yavanna (Mandor)
Written on Thu Feb 26 20:56:28 2004

I've been glaring at this zone for a while now, and this is what I have found.
I'm not asking for your approval for everything, this is merely what my
thoughts are right now, feel free to intervene, discuss or make your opinion
heard. Use at your own discretion:

--------------

:13,33,43,53,14,34,44,94,5,35,45,95,16,26,36,46,56,66,76,86,27,37,47,57,67,77,
87,38,48,58,29,39,49,59,69,79,89,99
     These rooms need explanations of why they have noexits. Nothing fancy,
     will be really easy, since the terrain is mostly mountains.

:6   I dont think a DT is needed (as the desc say), but a very difficult, very
     hurting fall would be better, with apropriate edescs of course. I think it
     should be both north and east.

:17  Same here, due north.

:16  Nothing fancy, merely a room where people fall into. dir_descs all around,
     describing the sheer cliff walls. And if we want to be _evil_, we put some
     lowlevel agg mob, hehe. Maybe a cottage against the mountain wall?

:109 I _really_ like this idea. I'd like to use special_door on both doors.
     Maybe not allow 'open' but rather some more elaborate command, like
     "part bushes" or so. Or hidden_exit together with something... A timed
     fall, and a fall if more than one enters would be nice. Mounts will of
     course refuse, or maybe they will be counted.

:23,24 and a few more.
     The road layout here isn't really working, I'll ponder the situation more.

:14,24,34,25,35,26,36
     This is easily resolved with /lib slope, good messages and harsh move
     penalties. Will make panicked fleeing persons suffer. Which is good.

--------------

Mobwise I will divide the area into 5 areas, namely:

1 The road/plains section in the northwest.
2 The plains and strea, in the northeast and mideast.
3 The road behemoth in the midwest and south.
4 The mountains in the southwest.
5 The mountains in the southeast.

1 This area is fairly flat, a bit dry but nourished in places. Birds, snakes,
  horses, patrols would like it. Wolves?
2 Plains, hills and a river. It's very green and lush, all animals should like
  it here. Plenty of bushes and trees.
3 Not really any animals at all, patrols, perhaps some snakes.
4 Goats. Birds, big ones. It's mostly mountiains here, high.
5 Goats, birds, orcs?

Other places, icedoor isn't very natural, so I wont touch it yet.

--------------

A few of the river rooms dont seem enterily correct, I'll fiddle around.

/ Mandor

Zone keyword "mobiles" (lgit: info/zones/188/mobiles):
New mobiles: no new mobs created for this zone.

Other mobs:

The zone can be divided into two parts so far as mobs are concerned. The bulk
of the higher level mobs are to be found in the "icedoor caves" which area has
basically been recreated (improved upon in terms of layout) from the old zone
93, which is to be replaced by z 188.

The remainder of the zone is populated by lower level mobs - boars, oxen,
birds,
snakes, rats, bats, mountain goats and ibex, bunnies, etc. A pack of grey
wolves
prowls, and by virtue of a starving and a rabid wolf in the pack, should show
some aggression.

The Misties run from northwest to southeast through the zone.

Zone keyword "boulders(mudlle)" (lgit: info/zones/188/boulders(mudlle)):
188:38 is a mountain room that overlooks a road through the mountain pass. It
will be set up as a very limited watch_tower, watching the road rooms along the
pass.

In this room there will be a number of boulders, small enough to be moved, yet
large enough that this will take some time and effort. The boulders can only
be pushed over the low-spot on the overlook, therefore only room 188:48 will 
be targeted by the trap.

When a player opts to "push boulder" a (slightly) delayed action will start -
it is interruptable if the player takes any other action (including simply 
hitting [rtn]) but if completed will drop a boulder onto the target room. There
is a (dex_checked) chance that any player or mob in the room below will avoid
being hit, but if they are hit they take quite serious damage. 

Once supply of boulders is exhausted, no more can be pushed over the edge.

Should be roughly analogous to Fornost oil pot.

This is in zone 182 - 
As the road now know as ABR was built, a small keep was built where is crossed
on of the tributarys to Bruinen. Small farms grew up around the castle. As the
evil once again began to move, the keep was deserted. It did not take long
until the forces of Sauron moved in, at first, old spirits and wraiths of the
long dead inhabitants, and later orcs, as Sauron started preparing for wars.
One of the earlier lords were buried just southeast of the keep, and his grave
was desecrated by the leader ob the orcs, trying out his magic in a foul

Elrond soon learned of the orcs living here, and sent two scouts to keep an

I've been glaring at this zone for a while now, and this is what I have found.
I'm not asking for your approval for everything, this is merely what my
thoughts are right now, feel free to intervene, discuss or make your opinion

     "part bushes" or so. Or hidden_exit together with something... A timed

Other places, icedoor isn't very natural, so I wont touch it yet.

/ Mandor

storyline.body:
step. To the south and west green hills can be reached, rising at least at
first with a barely
perceptible ascent from the plains. A small stream can be seen at some distance
to the northeast.
//line 2 replace "at least at" with "at"


on a@Lightly Wooded Hillside [188:62]
Tall, slender evergreens grow in abundance here, yet never drawing so close to
one-another as to
constitute a true forest. The ground alternates between a deep litter of old
pine needles close by
the trees, and thick, green grasses that bend in the wind that howls between
the trunks. An
occasional stump stands amid the grasses, covered with moss, and attesting to
the age of this
grove. The hills continue far into the south while slowly descending in the
west. To the north and
east the descent is more marked, as the hills give way to the plains that
stretch out below.
//line 3 replace "that howls"
//line 4 replace "far into" with "far to"


among some@Grassy Hills [188:63]
A few solitary pines stand amidst the medium sized grasses that cover the
hillsides here. The hills
continue in all directions, rolling off well into the distance. To the south
and east, far beyond
the hills, tall mountains rise into the sky.
//OK

among some@Grassy Hills [188:64]
The hills empty into a lush valley to the south and west. A few scattered trees
grow here on the
descending slopes of the hills, but not in any abundance. Far across the
valley, a tall mountainous
spur cuts the land from east to west, and it is this, together with the hills,
that have created
the rich vale that opens out not far to the south.
//OK

in the@Deep in a Lush Valley [188:65]
The valley extends for some miles both to the east and west, and reaches to the
foot of the
mountains in the south. The deep, loamy soil evidently has an ample supply of
water, for lush,
green grass covers the ground all around. A few scattered trees and many bushes
also dot the
landscape. This secluded valley would make excellent farmland if anyone were to
settle here. But as
it lies so very far from civilisation this would seem an unlikely prospect.
//OK


at a@Watering Hole [188:66]
Extending for several miles to the north, east and west, this lush valley comes
to an abrupt halt
here, its grassy floor marching right to the feet of a long mountain spur. The
cliffs loom high
above, but the vegetation still thrives here, despite the diminished access to
sunlight. A pool of
clear water has collected here surrounded by flourishing greenery.
//OK


on a@Narrow, Rocky Traverse [188:67]
A narrow, rock ledge curves along the base of some high mountain cliffs here,
offering a means of
travel between the rocky crags that extend to the south, and a steep, but
scalable ascent to the
west. The snow-capped peaks that reach high into the sky to the north and east
can barely be seen
from this vantage point.
//OK


@among the Mountains [188:68]
Riding is out of the question here. No discernible pathway can be seen along
these rocky slopes, so
the only option is to pick a way between the rocks and boulders, seeking out
the most level ground
as best is possible. Mighty peaks loom high above, their crests hidden from
sight amid the
billowing clouds.
//OK


@among the Mountains [188:69]
A low mountain range cuts through the area. The air that rolls down from those
heights is frigid,
and chilling to the bone. And the elements have taken their toll on the
landscape itself, with no
noticeable vegetation growing here at all. Rocks and boulders are all that
occupies these lonely
slopes.
//OK


at a@Shallow Crossing [188:70]
This part of the stream at first glance appears quite deep, but upon closer
inspection the bottom
silt can be made out quite clearly. The banks can be seen in the distance. It
is very cold and
clear as it runs by swiftly. The occasional school of minnows flits by and
larger darker shapes can
be discerned which can only be larger fish. The plains can be seen of to east
and west and beyond
them hills which eventually join a large mountain range to the south.
//line 2 replace "It is" with "The water is"
//line 4 replace "The plains can be seen of to east and west" with "Plains can
be seen to the east and west,"


on some@Marshy Ground [188:71]
The grasses turn a boggy carpet to the north and east where they draw closer to
a stream, and
diminish in health to the south. The landscape is remarkably flat in this
region, though some miles
to the south a range of hills rises up from the plains. To the east, the Misty
Mountains dominate
the horizon.
//OK


on some@Arid Plains [188:72]
The lands here are parched, despite their location between a lush stretch of
fields that lies near
a waterway to the north and east, and a band of grassy hills that crosses the
land running from
southeast to northwest, passing by not more than a couple of miles from here.
In this area, only a
few low, tussocks of dull, dry, yellow-brown grasses have managed to survive.
//note: complex first sentence.
//line 1 replace "that lies" with "lying"
//line 2 replace "that crosses the land running" with "crossing the land"
//line 3 replace "passing" with "which passes"


among some@Grassy Hills [188:73]
A small field can be seen over a slight rise here, while the slopes descend in
the north. The
slopes continue to roll further in the other directions. This slope is covered
with a scattering of
small trees and low brush, that are just enough to offer scant protection
against the winds and
rain, but not sufficient to afford any real shelter from the elements.
//note: "slope" repeated many times
//line 1 replace "the slopes descend in the north" with "the landscape descends
to"
//line 2 replace "This slope" with "This hillside"


among some@Grassy hills [188:74]
In the south the many peaks of the Misty Mountains are visible. Their tall
peaks reaching to the
clouds. A lush green valley lies before the mountains and these rolling hills
mark the northern
boundary of that lush land. Tumbling down toward the vale, the slope gradually
becomes grassier,
and the vegetation much greener.
//line 1 replace "visible. Their" with "visible, their"
//line 2 replace "before the mountains" with "to the south before the
mountains,"


in a@Lush Valley Nearing the Hills [188:75]
A few groves of tall trees dot the landscape, utilizing the excellent ground
and ample moisture.
The tall grass may hide wildlife, and there are trails worn in the grass that
indicate larger
animals make their way around here. The hills to the north can be reached from
here following a
sharp ascent and the mountains to the south rise up some distance away.
//OK


in a@Lush Valley by the Foot of a Cliff [188:76]
A lush valley extends out in all directions save to the south, where it runs
right to the foot of a
massive cliff. The mountain spur is only a low footnote to the Misty Mountains
that lie further
east, but the cliffs nonetheless afford this vale a good deal of protection
from the harsh weather
that blights much of the rest of the land hereabouts. As a result, the topsoil
is thicker and
richer here, supporting not only a thick sea of dark green grass, but also
scattered broadleaf
trees, and any number of low shrubs. A dense hedge of thorny bushes dominates
the land at the very
foot of the cliffs.
//OK


on a@Mountain Slope [188:77]
The mountain slope descends toward a high cliff to the north, whilst a taller
peak looms above to
the west. There is little protection here from the biting wind that blows
through the mountains
from the east. The stones here have been worn smooth and featureless from the
wind.
//note: adding reference to the ravineto the south
//line 2 replace "west." with "west. To the south, the mountainside is
interrupted by a chasm."
//line 3 replace "mountains" with "mountains,"
//line 4 replace "from the east. The stones here have been worn" with "and the
stones around are"
//line 4 replace "the wind." "the strong wind."


on a@Weathered Narrow Bridge [188:78]
The bridge spans a deep, rocky ravine. Built long ago by an unknown hand, it is
now so time-worn as
to be dilapidated. Flat and without any form of hand rails the bridge spans the
chasm as the wind
screams across it. The stonework has been sanded smooth by the incessant,
torturing wind.
//line 1 replace "hand rails" with "hand rails,"


@in the Mountains [188:79]
A wide ravine opens up to the north spanned by a decrepit bridge. East and
west, the mountain peaks
stretch out in a long chain that reaches far into the distance. To the
southeast the still higher
peaks of the Mountains of Moria reach even higher into the skies, their heads
shrouded in great,
grey, billowing clouds. Imposing cliffs loom above to the south and west, an
impenetrable barrier
to travel. Lesser slopes, that are strewn with boulders, but otherwise
passable, extend to the
north and east.
//line 1 replace "north" with "north,"
//line 3 replace "even higher" with "far up"


in a@Quiet Stream [188:80]
The water is crystal clear here with several large boulders providing some
deep, and almost still
pools near to either bank. Flowing from the south, the waters turn westward
here, but the current
is too languid to undercut the bank too much. Far to the south, beyond the dry
plains, hills join a
rocky mountain range.
//OK


in a@Lazy Stream [188:81]
The waters of a cold, clear stream cut across the plains, flowing here from
east to north. The
channel is rather wide at this point, and the water flows by so lazily that it
almost appears not
to move at all. The southern bank can be reached by means of some quick-footed
action over some
slippery looking boulders.
//OK


in some@Tall Grass [188:82]
The plains here are a collection of tall green grasses. It is obvious that the
stream feeds into
here and the ground has a slightly marshy feel to it. Water collects in
footprints left here. A
stream flows past this field to the east and north. To the south the ground
becomes harder as it
meets the slope of a hill. To the west the plains continue until they meet
hills.
//line 2 replace "here and" with "here, as"


among some@Grassy Hills [188:83]
These hills descend rapidly to the north and east while they rise steadily to
the south and west.
The land here is a sea of soft, green grass that stretches all the way down the
hillside to meet
what appear to be lush plains that lie to the north.
//line 1 replace "east while" with "east, while"


among some@Grassy Hills [188:84]
The rolling hills continue to the east, north and west of here, their grassy
slopes stretching off
into the distance. Grass grows in abundance in and among the many large
boulders that have come to
rest here. Down a gentle slope to the south a lush valley opens up, covered by
tall green grass.
And further in the distance, across the valley, a rocky spur of the Misty
Mountains can be seen
towering above everything.
//OK


in a@Lush Valley Nearing the Hills [188:85]
The valley is covered by tall grass here with some scattered green, broadleaf
trees growing here
and there. Nestling in the shelter of a range of hills that lies to the north,
and a mountain spur
to the south, these lands are quite well protected from the fiercest weather,
with the result that
vegetation flourishes throughout the vale.
//OK


in a@Lush Valley by the Foot of a Cliff [188:86]
A lush valley stretches to the north and west, its floor an ocean of tall, dark
green grasses that
wave gently in the wind. Protected to the north by a range of hills, and to the
south by the rising
mountains, this vale enjoys much milder weather conditions than most of the
nearby lands. A few
scattered broadleaf trees, and numerous low bushes thrive here, especially
nearing the feet of the
cliffs to the south and east, where a dense hedge of thorny shrubs has come to
dominate the
landscape.
//OK


@along a Mountain Slope [188:87]
The mountain slope is speckled with boulders, but for the most part the ground
here is fairly even.
The cliff to the north offers a view of the lands far below, though from this
height nothing can be
discerned in detail. East and west, this slope reaches along the spur, with
tall, a towering
mountain standing above the rest bars passage to the south. Many large boulders
lie upon the ground
here, split open by the cruel weather, or shattered as they have fallen from
the higher slopes.
//line 3 replace "with tall, a towering" with "with a tall, towering"
//line 4 replace "rest bars" with "rest and barring"


@atop a Whispering Mountain [188:88]
This mountain soars above the rest, only rising to greater heights to the east.
A basin has formed
here containing a frozen lake, and to the east an icy path can be discerned
climbing its way
further up the mountain. Winds carrying ice and snow flurry fiercely and while
voices in the air
mutter and scream endlessly.
//line 3 replace "fiercely and while" with "fiercely, while"


in the@Misty Mountains [188:89]
Rocky cliffs and mountain slopes abound to the east, their lofty, snow-clad
peaks reaching high
into the cloudy skies. The southern cliffs are sheer and slippery. Gentler
inclines to the east and
west offer a choice of routes from here, though in all cases the journey would
not be easy, the
uneven, always sloping ground strewn with loose rocks and boulders.
//OK


on some@Plains by a Stream [188:90]
The stream that flows by to the west has lent its life-giving waters to this
part of the plains,
making the lands lush and green. Large, broad leaf bushes compete with a sea of
tall grass to
define the landscape here. Far to the south a range of hills cuts across the
horizon, while to the
east the Misty Mountains dominate the vista.
//line 2 replace "broad leaf" with "broad-leaf"


in a@Deep Stream [188:91]
Lush, green grass can be seen growing along either bank of the stream, whose
waters flow from south
to west here. The stream bed is rather more rocky here than either upstream or
downstream, and so
the waters run much more rapidly, dancing and bouncing off the rocks as they
go. The water is very
cold and crystal clear, fed from run-offs from the mountain range to the east.
//OK


along a@Meandering Stream [188:92]
Curling with the contours of the lands that lie to the southeast, the stream
finally arrives here
from the distant mountains, to bring its cold, clear water to the plains. The
banks to either side
are alive with lush green grass and a proliferation of low bushes. Further off
to the west and
south, a range of hills can be seen on the horizon.
//line 1 replace "the stream finally arrives" with "a stream flows"
//line 2 replace "to bring" with "bringing"


in some@Green Brush [188:93]
These plains are slightly raised, with some of the run-off from the nearby hill
and mountain ranges
supplying much needed moisture. The vegetation is green and broad leaf bushes
grow in abundance
here. The bushes are hardy being themselves the only natural windbreak, in a
land where the
prevailing winds are cruel.
//line 2 replace "broad leaf" with "broad-leaf"
//line 3 replace "are hardy being themselves" with "are hardy, being "
//line 3 replace "windbreak," with "windbreak"


among some@Grassy Hills [188:94]
Scattered trees dot the landscape among these rolling hills, growing denser to
the east, where they
climb up the slopes of more hills. To the west and northwest, the hills
continue, their grassy
slopes receding far into the distance. As the slopes march down into the valley
below, to the
south, the grass becomes much longer, and the vegetation lusher.
//OK


at the@Edge of a Lush Valley [188:95]
The valley lies to the west, sheltered by mountains to the south and hills to
the north and east.
Long blades of dark green grass dance in the gentle wind, creating waves that
ripple across the
vale. To the south, a tall cliff face marks the starting point of a mountain
spur, an offshoot of
the Misty Mountains that dominate the horizon far to the east.
//OK


in a@Dry Channel [188:96]
No water flows now, but it appears that at some time in the past a stream ran
here, carving this
channel out of the living rock. Though the cliffs appear to offer no viable
route between the
plains and the mountain slopes, this ancient water course cuts back into them,
twisting and curving
its way between the valley and the heights above. The rock is fairly smooth,
but it should be
possible to travel this way, albeit only with considerable effort.
//line 2 replace "the cliffs" with "the cliffs to the south"


on the@Lower Slopes of a Spur [188:97]
A channel originating to the southeast runs on down the mountain to the north.
Perhaps it was once
the course of a stream, but it has long since run dry. Tall peaks loom above to
the east and south,
their snowy heads reaching far up into the clouds. The land slopes upward at a
more modest grade to
the west, along the flanks of this mountain spur.
//OK


on a@Howling Mountain [188:98]
Like a massive finger of stone, this tall peak reaches high into the skies. All
around the snowy
slopes fall away save far to the east where great peaks rage into the heavens.
To the south a
decline can be spotted worming its way down the mountain slopes. The air is
heavy with the sound of
strange voices chanting, whispering, cursing.
//line 2 replace "away save" with "away, save"


in the@Misty Mountains [188:99]
From the north the chill winds seem to increase dramatically, rolling down a
steep incline from the
peaks above as if intent only on making travel that way even harder. The wind
gusts down
rhythmically, sounding almost like the flap of giant wings. Though a fairly
gentle slope descends
to the west of here, the eastern and southern rock walls are impassable.
//line 1 replace "From the north" with "To the north"


@beneath the Mountain [188:100]
A natural cave has formed here. The grey walls are marred with streaks of brown
and black, and the
floor is uneven with rocks taking up almost every inch of space. To the north,
east and west it
appears there are adjoining caverns, but it is impossible to make out what is
in them from here.
//OK


in a@Stalagmite Cavern [188:101]
The hue of the rock here is that of a greyish, yellow colour. Great spires of
stone strike upwards
and downwards from the ceiling and floor. Pools of water cover the ground
allowing for little
movement save on a path that leads west. The shallow water glows with a faint,
iridescent green
light.
//line 1 replace "that of a greyish, yellow colour." with "turns to a greyish
yellow."


in a@Greystone Chamber [188:102]
Great slabs of rock, protruding from the walls, stab their way into the centre
of this cave. Like
knives piercing a skull, the rock slabs make it impossible to simply walk
straight through the
cave, instead demanding a zigzag route. North, east and west the walls close
in, and the only way
out lies south.
//OK


in a@White Stone Cavern [188:103]
The cavern walls here are composed of a white, speckled stone. One solid grey
rock leans against
the northern rockface, standing in stark contrast to the smooth marble walls. A
crack runs along
the ceiling of the passage. Nothing can be seen behind the darkness that lives
in the crack.
//line 2 replace "rockface, standing" with "rockface, and a black slab covers
part of the pavement. Both are"


in a@Partially Caved-in Passage [188:104]
Boulders dominate the floor of the tunnel with large pockets of space clearly
visible in the
ceiling from whence they undoubtedly came. The majority of the fallen stones
are piled up in the
northeast part of the tunnel causing the entire area to be tilted. The
composition of the stone is
unclear, but it crumbles quite easily. The tunnel bends sharply north and east.
//note: "tunnel" repeated many times
//line 1 replace "tunnel with" with "tunnel, with"
//line 3 replace "of the tunnel" with "of the passage"
//line 3 replace "The composition of the stone" with "The stones composition"


at a@Gaping Chasm [188:105]
A huge pit cuts through the floor of this cave. Stretching several yards in
length, it would be
impossible to cross if it wasn't for the crude, rope bridge stretched across
it. Darkness rises up
from the depths of the chasm like a cloud, and at the bottom, a void devours
all knowledge of what
could be known of that place.
//OK

in a@Dark Grotto [188:106]
A stone arch, in defiance of nature and time, stands alone in the centre of the
cave. The walls are
made of a blackish stone with veins of some silvery rock branching up to the
ceiling. Much of the
dark stone that comprises the walls has fallen to the ground creating a black
shroud along the
outer edges of the cavern.
//line 2 replace "veins of some silvery rock" with "some silvery veins"


in a@Black Cavern [188:107]
Glistening rivers of obsidian stone writhe their way up the walls, intertwining
throughout the
rocky strata. The cave, much like a horrible black mouth, has stalactites and
stalagmites scattered
haphazardly throughout the rounded walls, and extends off to the west and
south. Naturally formed
steps provide a path to what appears to be a cave above this one.
//OK

in a@Smoky Cave [188:108]
Considerably warmer than the neighbouring cavern, this cave abruptly leads to a
dead end. Piles of
charred stones are scattered here and there bleeding a choking smoke from
beneath. It is difficult
to see through the haze and the scent of burning cracked rock fills the
nostrils.
//OK

in a@Troll Hall [188:109]
Complete darkness reigns supreme within these mountains. This great cavern
seems have been roughly
cut into the mountain. Crude, dark murals span the walls, depicting scenes of
violence and
debauchery. They appear to be painted with a strangely red, viscous liquid.
//OK

in a@Bone Heap [188:110]
An overpowering odour rifles through the air, stripping it of any semblance of
nature. Great piles
of gnawed bones litter the floor, with one particularly massive heap laying
claim to the centre of
the room. This place wears death like a heavy cloak. Occasionally, the bones
seem to move, as if
something was crawling under the surface.
//OK


@beneath the Stalactites [188:111]
Smaller than most, this cave is bone chillingly cold and tight. Its ceiling is
low and very uneven
with large, jagged rocks jutting down in many places. The floor is similarly
rugged with scattered
boulders and large holes all around. A gaping fissure in the floor leads into
some blackness below.
//line 1 replace "bone chillingly" with "bone-chillingly"


in a@Naturally Formed Passage [188:112]
Inside this fissure of rock, shelves of limestone form a scaffolding that might
be possible to
scale. Up above it is difficult to see a path forward as stalactites hang down
blocking vision in
that direction, but perhaps a small hole is visible. To the west a very narrow
opening can be
spotted; maybe it is big enough to squeeze through.
//OK


in a@Narrow Crawlspace [188:113]
The ceiling of this little space hangs low making it difficult to pass through
comfortably while
the floor slants upward. The limestone walls crumble and trickle shards of rock
onto the ground
even if they are lightly brushed. Westwards the path seems to become quite
difficult while the path
east a bit more open.
//line 1 replace "low making" with "low, making"
//line 3 replace "even if they are lightly brushed" with "at the slightest
touch"
//line 3 replace "difficult while" with "difficult, while"
//line 4 replace "east" with "east is"


in a@Cramped Cave [188:114]
The cavern opens up a little to give some standing room. To the east an
extremely cramped passage
can be seen disappearing into the rock while to the north and south two more
caves connect with
this one. The air is still and stale; nothing breathes here.
//OK


in the@Chamber of Echoes [188:115]
Shale covers the walls of this rocky hole in the mountain. Soft echoes whisper
through the cavern
emanating from who knows where. The stone supporting this cave stand smooth and
strong but to the
west they seem a bit more brittle and textured.
//line 2 replace "stand" with "stands"
//line 3 replace "they seem a bit more brittle and textured." with "it seems a
bit more textured and brittle."


in a@Low Cavern [188:116]
The ceiling here dips a bit making this cavern a bit shallow. The walls, now
the texture of granite
slides into the floor making standing space scarce. The nooks and crevices
travel deep into the
walls causing numerous black holes to be peeping out of the rock.
//line 1 replace "dips a bit" with "dips a bit,"
//line 1 replace "a bit shallow" with "somewhat cramped"
//line 1 replace "the texture of granite" with "now having granite-like
texture,"
//line 2 replace "slides into" with "curve toward""


in a@Cave under the Mountain [188:117]
The cave is tall and wide. In the centre a great chunk of rock has fallen from
above and rests like
a stone table in the middle of the room. Above, there is an opening from whence
this boulder must
have come from. The walls of this cavern are studded with twinkling stones
guarding the secrets.
//line 1 replace "The cave is tall and wide. In the centre" with "In the centre
of this tall and wide cave,"
//line 2 replace "table in the middle of the room." with "table." because it
already said it's in the center
//line 2 replace "from whence" with "whence" because it already means "from
where"
//line 3 replace "The walls of this cavern" with "The walls"
//line 2 replace "the secrets." with "any secret, dark crevice."


in a@Tunnel in the Dark [188:118]
A roughly cut tunnel stands here. Deep in the dark the tunnel curves itself
around eventually
twisting a path to the north. While clearly hewn from the rock, this passage
seems to have not been
touched by the hand of a living thing in at least an age.
//line 1 replace "the tunnel curves itself around" with "it curves around,"


in a@Disused Tunnel [188:119]
No natural light has ever reached this place that lies deep beneath the Misty
Mountains. The rough
tunnel walls bear no distinctive features, and it seems it would be very easy
to get lost within
these caverns. But from here the choice of route is rather limited: the tunnel
stretches west,
south and north.
//line 1 replace "No natural light has ever reached this place that lies deep
beneath the Misty Mountains"

Keyword "superzone-storyline" (lgit: info/zones/188/superzone-storyline)

Superzone storyline for the zones 184 - 188 + 317 - 319.
30-Sep-2020, Orlanth

INTRODUCTION
============
These zones were already finished many years ago, but they were doomed to be
too open by Timodeus, as far as what I know about it. The plan is to make these
zones more bottlenecked, especially the road, so it's more dangerous to travel,
while still leaving some options for the travellers. We will also add new caves
and camps to lure players to explore the area. Compared to the current ABR 
zones, these zones will follow the grid map closely, and they will be full
sized 
zones (they are already built like that).

The zones won't have much safe spots for players, apart from trolls that will
have icedoor caves like they have now. Most of the mobs will be aggressive to
all races. There is one camp that can be switched to the race sides similarly
to
some switchable towers.

These zones will replace the current Ancient Broken Road zones 31, 23, 92 and
93.

PLANNED MAP CHANGES
===================

CURRENT ABR LAYOUT:

        68----181
        |     |
        |     |
        183---182
        |     |
        |     |
        31----30
        |
        |
        23
        |
        |
        92
        |
        |
        93
        |
        |
158 ----94


NEW ABR LAYOUT:

       68----181
       |     |
       |     |
       183---182
       |     |
       |     |
       184---30
       |     |
       |     |
186----185---317
|      |    /
|      |   /
187----318-
|      |
|      |
188 ---319
|      |
|      |
158----94



94 is Khuzur zone.
31 is current ABR tower zone.
182 is Brolg zone.

GENERAL INFO
============
These zones have an important road that is used by all races to walk along the
Misty Mountains. There are no great places to cross the mountains, except in
Redhorn Pass and in the north the trail that goes through the mountains.
Hundreds of years ago these areas had people living here, farming and tending
for livestock. Now the area is too dangerous for people to live, there are
orcs and goblins in the mountains, and even robbers stalking for unwary
travellers. Still, the route is also important for Elrond and Galadriel, and
they want to keep the road open for elves to travel. They have sent some scouts
to the area, to keep watch for enemies. Elrond has also asked DÃºnedain to help
with guarding the area. Sauron is naturally opposing this, hence the presence
of evil beings. One of the places where the good, evil and foul fight for
power, is the switchable camp the zone 187. Bandits and smugglers are also
infesting the area, they have their own camp in the ruins in the zone 185.

In the south in the mountains in the zone 188, there is a hidden DÃºnedain
outpost. From there they are watching the pass in ABR for enemies. If the 
switchable camp is occupied by DÃºnedain, they will send a patrol to intercept 
bigger enemy groups.
In the superzone, there are five fire beacons that DÃºnedain use to signal that
enemy is approaching. Using this method, they try to control the area by
intercepting and blocking the road.

Who is controlling the camp, will also have a superzone wide effect in mob
loads and ambushing patrols. For example, goblins may also block the road
if they are given the chance. In this case, DÃºnedain will have to fall back to
their hidden outpost to collect forces. Similarly, orcs may control the area,
if
players manage to turn the camp to orkish.

There is a huge network of tunnels in the Misty Mountains to the east of the
road. A small tribe of goblins has inhabited these caves and tunnels for many
years now. The goblins are also sneaking outside and harassing travellers.
These goblins don't mind if you are an orc or an elf, they will attack
everyone.
If the switchable camp is not controlled by any player forces, the goblins will
take over. In the mountains, there used to be some dwarven tunnels in the past,
and these tunnels still exist. A secret hidden dwarven tomb is deep in the
caves 
but it's hard to access. There will be goblins on the way! Luckily goblins have
not been able to access the tombs yet, the dwarves in the past build the tombs 
so well and put so good defences that they dare not to go there.

The Misty Mountains also have more tunnels than the ones occupied by the
goblins. These tunnels will have new, nasty, aggressive to all trolls. They are
not friends with goblins or anyone else. From these tunnels, there is an access
further into the mountains. There, deep in these snowy mountains, there is an
area that is inhabited by dangerous, huge snow giants, and by their fearless
leader Jotnir.

PLAINS
------
Outside of the road, most of the zones consist of plains, there are some hills
and mountains in the zones too. The road is kind of blocked for gameplay 
reasons, can be justified by thorny bushes and hedges. But around the road 
there are lots of plains. The plains itself are also divided by natural
formations 
in some areas. There are only a few forest rooms in these zones. The plains 
would mostly have some animals wandering in the area, but also, some 
aggressive mobs like wargs. Black sorcerer would also find a new home in
 these zones. We are also considering to add one stabber mob, something
 like Vairr or experienced trapper around Tharbad. Some orkish warg-riders 
may also find their home somewhere in the zones, at least probably in the 
northern parts.

A list of possible mobiles for the plains:
Animals (too many to list here)
6814    an orkish warg-rider
1177    a starving warg
6101    a ferocious warg
7303    a huge warg
5550    a black sorcerer
6812    an orkish scout
1471    a massive tangle of roots
1804    a clump of roots
5006    a mass of vines
6911    a thick tangle of vines

A list of possible plants for the plains:
709    a cluster of yellow flowers
711    a mass of dark green leaves, a wall climber plant
6012   a large rose bush
8260   a handful of clover
8283   a sturdy flowering plant (comfrey), grows best in sun, moist environment
8288   a foul-smelling root (valerian)
8301   a bushy flowering plant (foxtail, extremely rare)
8302   a slender plant (foxglove, very rare)
8305   a sweetly-smelling shrub (extremely rare, load o8268 in it)
8308   a many-branched shrub (thyme, produces o8273 when crushed)
8309   a bright green shrub (coriander, rare, loads o8255 as leaves)
8310   a woody, many-stemmed plant (rosemary, load in full sun and sandy soil,
produces o8272 when crushed)
8311   a woody, stemmed plant (tarragon, lightly wooded plaints with sun,
produces o8253 when crushed)
8312   a thin, hairy plant (marjoram, produces o8259 when crushed)
8313   a short evergreen (juniper, loads o8274 berries)
8318   some white, egg-shaped berries
8321   a shrub with maple-like leaves (blackcurrant bush, loads o1495)
8323   a large thorn branched shrub (blackberry, loads o8009)
8332   an erect shrub with green pinnate leaves (raspberry, loads o8331)
8333   a stinging nettle (bushy areas or brush)


RIVERS
------
We have quite a many river rooms in these zones. The rivers are also made
more constrained, they have one ways and rapids to make using them for
escaping from pk harder. The water is flowing down from the misty mountains
that reside to the east of these zones. These are smaller rivers that will join
to river Bruinen that flows more to the west.

Mobs would be mostly fishes, and maybe water snakes.

A list of possible plants for the shallows:
o710    a slender-stemmed plant, grows in muddy land or shallow waters
o712    a prickly plant with blue flower heads, shallows
o713    a bundle of fresh-scented leaves
o1752   a water lily
o8303   a tall, grey-green plant (figwort, very rare)
o8344   a many-branched stem of bright yellow flowers (ragwort)


MOUNTAINS
---------
The zone 188 and some of the corner zones have mountain rooms in this range
of zones. We will probably be creating some new giant mobs to the mountains.
Such giants that like to live in cold climate.

A list of possible mobs for the mountains:
6011     a mountain ibex
9400     a mountain ibex
1431     a young mountain lion
1480     a mountain lioness
1481     a mountain lion
9200     a mountain goat
7103     a mountain troll

CAVES
-----
There will be huge new caves system that will have new goblin mobs.
Then there will be the old icedoor caves, that has trolls.

A list of possible mobs for the caves:
spiders, trolls, orcs, demon wolves, smugglers, brigands maybe.

CAMPS
-----
There is a camp in the zone 187 that will have switchable mobs, DÃºnedain,
orcs, zaugurz orcs or goblins. Goblins mean in this case = wilderness.


MOBS TO BE REMOVED
------------------
Compared to the current zones I would remove following mobs:
- spirit type mobs
- the illusionist


OBJECTS
-------
What kind of EQ will load in the area. TBD.


MUDLLES
-------
These zones already have some custom mudlles installed. Plan is to add as few
mudlles as is possible, so we try to keep it simple.


INTERESTING FEATURES
--------------------
The zones would still have a black altar as before.

These zones were already finished many years ago, but they were doomed to be
too open by Timodeus, as far as what I know about it. The plan is to make these
zones more bottlenecked, especially the road, so it's more dangerous to travel,
while still leaving some options for the travellers. We will also add new caves
and camps to lure players to explore the area. Compared to the current ABR 
zones, these zones will follow the grid map closely, and they will be full
sized 
zones (they are already built like that).

The zones won't have much safe spots for players, apart from trolls that will
have icedoor caves like they have now. Most of the mobs will be aggressive to
all races. There is one camp that can be switched to the race sides similarly
to
some switchable towers.

These zones will replace the current Ancient Broken Road zones 31, 23, 92 and
93.

GENERAL INFO
============
These zones have an important road that is used by all races to walk along the
Misty Mountains. There are no great places to cross the mountains, except in
Redhorn Pass and in the north the trail that goes through the mountains.
Hundreds of years ago these areas had people living here, farming and tending
for livestock. Now the area is too dangerous for people to live, there are
orcs and goblins in the mountains, and even robbers stalking for unwary
travellers. Still, the route is also important for Elrond and Galadriel, and
they want to keep the road open for elves to travel. They have sent some scouts
to the area, to keep watch for enemies. Elrond has also asked DÃºnedain to help
with guarding the area. Sauron is naturally opposing this, hence the presence
of evil beings. One of the places where the good, evil and foul fight for
power, is the switchable camp the zone 187. Bandits and smugglers are also
infesting the area, they have their own camp in the ruins in the zone 185.

In the south in the mountains in the zone 188, there is a hidden DÃºnedain
outpost. From there they are watching the pass in ABR for enemies. If the 
switchable camp is occupied by DÃºnedain, they will send a patrol to intercept 
bigger enemy groups.
In the superzone, there are five fire beacons that DÃºnedain use to signal that
enemy is approaching. Using this method, they try to control the area by
intercepting and blocking the road.

Who is controlling the camp, will also have a superzone wide effect in mob
loads and ambushing patrols. For example, goblins may also block the road
if they are given the chance. In this case, DÃºnedain will have to fall back to
their hidden outpost to collect forces. Similarly, orcs may control the area,
if
players manage to turn the camp to orkish.

There is a huge network of tunnels in the Misty Mountains to the east of the
road. A small tribe of goblins has inhabited these caves and tunnels for many
years now. The goblins are also sneaking outside and harassing travellers.
These goblins don't mind if you are an orc or an elf, they will attack
everyone.
If the switchable camp is not controlled by any player forces, the goblins will
take over. In the mountains, there used to be some dwarven tunnels in the past,
and these tunnels still exist. A secret hidden dwarven tomb is deep in the
caves 
but it's hard to access. There will be goblins on the way! Luckily goblins have
not been able to access the tombs yet, the dwarves in the past build the tombs 
so well and put so good defences that they dare not to go there.

The Misty Mountains also have more tunnels than the ones occupied by the
goblins. These tunnels will have new, nasty, aggressive to all trolls. They are
not friends with goblins or anyone else. From these tunnels, there is an access
further into the mountains. There, deep in these snowy mountains, there is an
area that is inhabited by dangerous, huge snow giants, and by their fearless
leader Jotnir.

PLAINS
------
Outside of the road, most of the zones consist of plains, there are some hills
and mountains in the zones too. The road is kind of blocked for gameplay 
reasons, can be justified by thorny bushes and hedges. But around the road 
there are lots of plains. The plains itself are also divided by natural
formations 
in some areas. There are only a few forest rooms in these zones. The plains 
would mostly have some animals wandering in the area, but also, some 
aggressive mobs like wargs. Black sorcerer would also find a new home in
 these zones. We are also considering to add one stabber mob, something
 like Vairr or experienced trapper around Tharbad. Some orkish warg-riders 
may also find their home somewhere in the zones, at least probably in the 
northern parts.

RIVERS
------
We have quite a many river rooms in these zones. The rivers are also made
more constrained, they have one ways and rapids to make using them for
escaping from pk harder. The water is flowing down from the misty mountains
that reside to the east of these zones. These are smaller rivers that will join
to river Bruinen that flows more to the west.

Mobs would be mostly fishes, and maybe water snakes.

A list of possible plants for the shallows:
o710    a slender-stemmed plant, grows in muddy land or shallow waters
o712    a prickly plant with blue flower heads, shallows
o713    a bundle of fresh-scented leaves
o1752   a water lily
o8303   a tall, grey-green plant (figwort, very rare)
o8344   a many-branched stem of bright yellow flowers (ragwort)


MOUNTAINS
---------
The zone 188 and some of the corner zones have mountain rooms in this range
of zones. We will probably be creating some new giant mobs to the mountains.
Such giants that like to live in cold climate.

A list of possible mobs for the mountains:
6011     a mountain ibex
9400     a mountain ibex
1431     a young mountain lion
1480     a mountain lioness
1481     a mountain lion
9200     a mountain goat
7103     a mountain troll

CAVES
-----
There will be huge new caves system that will have new goblin mobs.
Then there will be the old icedoor caves, that has trolls.

A list of possible mobs for the caves:
spiders, trolls, orcs, demon wolves, smugglers, brigands maybe.

CAMPS
-----
There is a camp in the zone 187 that will have switchable mobs, DÃºnedain,
orcs, zaugurz orcs or goblins. Goblins mean in this case = wilderness.


MOBS TO BE REMOVED
------------------
Compared to the current zones I would remove following mobs:
- spirit type mobs
- the illusionist


OBJECTS
-------
What kind of EQ will load in the area. TBD.


MUDLLES
-------
These zones already have some custom mudlles installed. Plan is to add as few
mudlles as is possible, so we try to keep it simple.


INTERESTING FEATURES
--------------------
The zones would still have a black altar as before.
